div.div:
The build fails, with the rule spelled out
Allowed: add an optional field with a default, widen a union.
Not allowed: remove a field, rename a field, change a type, add a mandatory field without a default, make an optional field mandatory, remove an enum symbol.
Accepting a deliberate break is an explicit action that produces a reviewable diff:
./gradlew updateSchemaBaseline

div.div:
Why FULL rather than BACKWARD
BACKWARD alone permits field removal, because a new reader simply ignores the dropped field. The stated evolution policy is new optional fields with defaults, no removal, no type changes, and only FULL enforces that as written.
FULL is also what a rolling upgrade needs: two schema versions are live at once, and an old consumer must still read a new producer's output.

display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
One definition, not two
EnrichedTradeEvent embeds TradeEvent. It registers as a reference:
trades.enriched EnrichedTradeEvent.avsc
dev.engnotes.fes.events.TradeEvent=trades.raw-value
Inlining the type would give the registry two definitions of one record and let them drift. Referenced subjects are listed first in subjects.tsv so the version resolves.

div.div:
What the numbers are today
16 schema files · 31 generated Java types · 19 registered subjects, being 15 domain subjects plus 4 dead-letter subjects, all four carrying DeadLetterEvent
Deliberately absent: legacy.trades.cdc carries the Debezium connector's own envelope rather than a schema this repository owns, and remediation.requested and precedent.graph.sync have no schema yet.
